title: Chess Hydration Strategy Lab
description: An interactive educational exhibit where students learn about cognitive performance and hydration science. A chess board (ABeautifulGame) sits on a virtual lab table alongside a water bottle (WaterBottle). Students must conduct a simulated experiment by configuring hydration levels, selecting chess pieces to test cognitive tasks, and observing how dehydration affects strategic thinking performance through animated visualizations.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements an interactive 3D educational lab about hydration and cognitive performance. Load both GLB models using GLTFLoader: place ABeautifulGame.glb (chess set) centered on a flat table surface and WaterBottle.glb to its right, both scaled appropriately to coexist naturally. Use a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 3, 5) looking at the table center. Add ambient light (intensity 0.6), a directional light from upper-left, and a subtle point light near the water bottle with a blue tint. Render a simple table plane beneath the models. Create an HTML overlay panel titled 'Cognitive Hydration Lab' with these sequential interactions: (1) A slider labeled 'Hydration Level' (0-100%) that adjusts the water bottle's vertical fill by scaling/translating a semi-transparent blue plane inside or near the bottle. (2) Three clickable chess pieces on the board that highlight with emissive glow when hovered using raycasting — clicking one selects it as the 'test subject' and lifts it slightly with a tween animation. (3) A 'Run Trial' button that triggers an animated sequence: the selected piece moves in a pattern on the board (speed proportional to hydration level — higher hydration means faster, smoother movement). (4) A dynamic bar chart overlay (HTML/CSS) showing 'Reaction Time', 'Accuracy', and 'Focus Score' metrics that populate with randomized values weighted by the hydration slider value. (5) A 'Record Data' button that logs each trial to a visible data table below the viewport. (6) After 3+ recorded trials, enable a 'Analyze Results' button that highlights the best-performing trial row in green and displays a conclusion sentence about optimal hydration. Use OrbitControls for camera interaction. Validate that hydration is set, a piece is selected, and at least 3 trials are recorded before enabling analysis. Add smooth CSS transitions on all UI elements.
